text: Vietnam-South Korea-France consortium wins North-South high-speed railway feasibility study and basic design contract

After a long search for an international consultancy unit, the North-South high-speed railway project has identified a consortium of eight companies to undertake the survey, feasibility study report, overall technical design, and bidding document preparation.

According to contractor selection results for package TV-02, announced on November 22, the selected consortium comprises eight companies from Vietnam, South Korea, and France, with the approved bid price of over VND10.243 trillion (approximately $375 million), and with a project duration of 30 months.

This is one of the large-scale consultancy packages playing a crucial role in the investment preparation process for the high-speed railway project, with a preliminary total investment estimated at approximately $67.34 billion.
The winning consortium comprises eight companies, with SYSTRA from France as the leading member.
The South Korean companies involved are Sambo Engineering, Yooshin Engineering Corporation, and Korea National Railway (KNR).

On the Vietnamese side, there are four companies: Transport Engineering Design Inc. (TEDI), Southern Transport Engineering Design Joint Stock Company (TEDI SOUTH), Transport Investment and Construction Consultancy Joint Stock Company (TRICC), and Hoang Long Construction Consultancy Joint Stock Company (HOANG LONG).
This package is part of the contractor selection plan for several packages in the investment preparation phase of the North-South high-speed railway project.
According to Mr. Pham Huu Son, Chairman of TEDI, Vietnamese contractors will undertake a relatively large volume of work in package TV-02.

These companies have accumulated experience through participating in the design consultancy of several railway projects, including the Hanoi-Quang Ninh high-speed railway and the Ben Thanh-Can Gio line.

The participation of four domestic consultancy companies in the consortium with international partners demonstrates the presence of Vietnamese consultancy forces in an infrastructure project with particularly high technical requirements.

However, the effectiveness of this cooperation will depend on the actual scope of work, the level of professional involvement, and the ability to absorb experience and technology from foreign partners during implementation.
According to published information, the consortium was the only bidder when the package closed at 9 a.m. on November 9, 2026.
The package had an estimated price of over VND 10.782 trillion and was organized for contractor selection through the usual international bidding method.

After approving the contractor selection results, the Thang Long Project Management Board - the investor for the North-South high-speed railway project, and the consortium will proceed with negotiations.
The negotiation results will form the basis for the parties to sign a contract to implement the work.
The approval of the contractor selection results does not yet mean that the contract has officially taken effect.

According to the requirements of the Thang Long Project Management Board, package TV-02 includes surveying, preparing a feasibility study report, overall technical design (FEED), and bidding document preparation.
These tasks are crucial for determining the investment plan, technical scale, and basis for implementing subsequent project packages.
An important requirement is that within 12 months from the effective date of the contract, the consultancy unit must complete the mid-term feasibility study report.
In this report, the route must be stably determined, and key control points such as station, bridge, and tunnel locations must be clarified.
The report must also propose technological options for submission to competent authorities for review, appraisal, and decision-making.
The research process must ensure technical requirements while harmonizing with local planning, minimizing impacts on the lives and activities of people in areas where the railway passes through.

According to the plan, after about 15-18 months from the effective date of the consultancy contract, some component projects that meet the conditions will be researched and proposed to expedite implementation procedures, aiming for early commencement.

The construction of stations in major cities such as Ngoc Hoi Station (Hanoi) and Thu Thiem Station (Ho Chi Minh City) is prioritized for early implementation, expected by the end of 2027 or early 2028.

The preparation of these stations is also linked to the requirement for synchronized connection with the urban railway system and urban development orientation according to the public transport model.
Alongside the preparation of the feasibility study report, land clearance preparation is also being accelerated.

For sections where the route has been clearly determined, the Thang Long Project Management Board and the consultancy unit will report to the Ministry of Construction for consideration, allowing for the implementation of land clearance stakes, which will then be handed over to localities for organization.
The goal is to complete the handover of stakes to localities within 3 months from the approval of the mid-term report, expected in the fourth quarter of 2027.

The North-South high-speed railway project spans approximately 1,541 km, starting at Ngoc Hoi Station (Hanoi) and ending at Thu Thiem Station (Ho Chi Minh City), passing through 15 provinces and cities.
The line is planned for new double-track investment, with a gauge of 1,435 mm, a design speed of 350 km/h, a load of 22.5 tons/axle, with 23 passenger stations and 5 freight stations.
The preliminary total investment for the project is estimated at approximately $67.34 billion.
